description: Every action defined in policies/adversarial.yaml, grouped against the Spring Data reference harness. 'conformance' actions must match the check() oracle. 'adapterUnsupported' lists conformance actions an adapter cannot express and must reject loudly. 'expectedUnsupported' lists shapes rejected by the reference; 'adapterSupportedExpected' records adapters that intentionally translate one of those shapes. 'knownDivergences' records upstream planner behavior that prevents an oracle comparison.

prisma.reason: Prisma emits LIKE without an ESCAPE clause and does not escape wildcards, so a needle containing % or _ cannot be matched literally; the adapter throws instead of filtering wrong
Same LIKE-wildcard limitation as like-percent
The folded needle is '100%', hitting the same LIKE-wildcard limitation as like-percent
A column-valued needle would need per-row LIKE escaping, which Prisma filters cannot express; the adapter throws
Same column-needle LIKE limitation as f2f-contains
Same column-needle LIKE limitation as f2f-contains
Prisma field references only work between fields of the same model; comparing an element column with an outer column is cross-model, so the adapter throws
Cross-model comparison plus the column-needle LIKE limitation
Contains a cross-model element-vs-outer column comparison (t.name == R.attr.aString)
Arithmetic on both sides of a comparison cannot be solved to a plain column filter; Prisma filters cannot express column arithmetic
Division by a column cannot be solved to a plain column filter
Prisma where-filters cannot express relation-count thresholds (only empty/non-empty via none/some)
Same relation-count limitation as size-threshold
Prisma has no string-length filter
Same relation-count limitation as size-threshold
Same relation-count limitation as size-threshold
Embeds a size(...) == 1 count threshold; same limitation as size-threshold
exists_one requires counting matching elements, which Prisma where-filters cannot express; the adapter throws instead of silently degrading to exists
Same exists_one counting limitation
Prisma filters cannot express column arithmetic, and algebraically solving fractional IEEE-754 addition is not reversible for every row
Same fractional column-arithmetic limitation as arith-add-eq-frac
An exact corpus witness does not make the general column-addition predicate expressible; Prisma has no column arithmetic
Prisma has no string-length filter, so a giant size threshold remains inexpressible
Same string-length limitation as size-huge-gt
Hierarchy descendant prefixes require literal LIKE matching, but Prisma string filters cannot escape % or _; the adapter throws instead of treating them as wildcards
Comparing a related element column with an outer scalar column is cross-model, while Prisma field references are same-model only
Same cross-model correlated comparison limitation as in-var-var, under negation

sqlalchemy.reason: SQLAlchemy's SQLite dialect supplies REGEXP support, and the adapter translates matches() through that database capability

knownDivergences.reason: The planner folds has(unknown attr) to KIND_ALWAYS_ALLOWED (a Cerbos planner bug, not an adapter bug), so the adapter returns all rows while check() denies rows where the attribute is missing. Excluded from the oracle run rather than asserted against.
